chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not wear a ring [for sealing] other than silver, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The palm is not purified wherein is a ring of iron'.

key_terms.تَخَتَّمُوا: to wear a ring for sealing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing an iron ring in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the preference for silver rings in Shia jurisprudence by linking the Imams' practice to the Prophet and Amir al-Mu'minin, while noting the prohibition of iron due to its association with impurity or lack of purification. It reflects the broader scholarly tradition of distinguishing between noble metals for adornment and sealing, emphasizing ritual cleanliness (taharah) in personal accessories. The chain of transmission highlights the continuity of this ruling from the Prophet through the Imams, reinforcing its authenticity in Shia legal thought.
